node_definition.done_when: Read section 31 of crew-observability-truth first; its evidence is run r-20261002T124430828085-ctta-tree-capacity-on-critical-nodes, whose attempt-3-exit.json recorded exit_code 1 three seconds after launch while worker pid 1184382 lived on. The supervisor exit record (_supervisor_exit_record in reckon/crew/dispatch.py, and the supervisor in reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py) is never written for an attempt whose launched worker process is still alive. When the immediate child exits first, the supervisor waits for the worker, or records the attempt as still running with the worker's pid, never as exited. tests/test_attempt_exit_waits_for_its_worker.py drives a supervisor whose immediate child exits while the worker it started keeps running, in a temporary RECKON_HOME. It asserts no exit record is written until the worker ends, and that the record written afterwards carries the worker's exit. Keep the worker process in the test bounded by its own timeout, and end it from the test by its pid. The resume half of section 31 is a separate node; do not change resume code. Existing tests that reach _supervisor_exit_record or supervisor_main keep passing: grep tests/ for both names to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/attempt-exit-waits-for-its-worker.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
